transcript:
Meeting start: 2025-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Pioneer Head of ML), Liam O'Sullivan (Plat Eng), Rita Gomez (InfoSec)

SUMMARY (auto): Quick alignment on POC success criteria and who owns which acceptance tests. Agreed on p50/p95 latency targets, throughput baselines, and quality sampling. Decided reporting as a CSV + short PDF summary with per-route metrics + example prompts.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call, then, uh, we'll go through the success criteria doc.
[00:08] Maya: Hey Samir, hi Elena. Thanks. We got, uh, the doc you sent, we've got a few comments but overall looks good.
[00:15] Elena: Great. I can walk through the acceptance tests and how we'll run the benchmarks; Samir will talk timelines and procurement notes.
[00:22] Liam: Quick note from infra — we need the VPC peering window on your side, we have maintenance windows 12/16-12/18 so prefer benchmarks outside that.
[00:30] Rita: And security will need SOC2 or at least scoping artifact before we start any data access.
[00:36] Samir: Absolutely — we'll attach SOC2 and our network diagram. On to success criteria: we've proposed four buckets — performance (latency/throughput), reliability/error rates, cost targets, and quality checks (sampling against golden set).
[00:50] Maya: For latency, our user-facing SLO is p95 < 800ms on our current hosted endpoint. We don't expect Redwood to necessarily match exactly, but for the POC we need clear go/no-go.
[01:00] Elena: Proposed POC thresholds: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 700ms for the medium-size prompt set (avg 180 tokens), p95 < 1200ms for long prompts (avg 600 tokens) — do those map to what you saw in our perf deck?
[01:18] Maya: Yeah those are in the ballpark. Our main concern is tail latency; we run a lot of interactive queries.
[01:25] Samir: Noted. For throughput, are you aiming for sustained X qps or bursty peaks?
[01:30] Liam: Sustained ~25 RPS for inference across 3 services, peaks up to 80 RPS for short bursts.
[01:37] Elena: Ok so we'll define baseline throughput test: 25 RPS sustained over a 10-minute window and a burst test 80 RPS for 2 minutes.
[01:45] Samir: Error budget — we recommend <0.5% HTTP 5xx during tests, and any model rejects or length truncations counted separately.
[01:53] Maya: For quality, we have a golden set of 500 prompts with expected outputs and scoring thresholds — we want exact or semantically similar answers; propose BLEU >= 0.6 and human sample pass rate >= 85% on a 100-sample manual review.
[02:08] Elena: We'll wire up the golden set to the acceptance harness; we'll run automatic scoring and then a human review for the 100-sample set.
[02:16] Liam: Cost — we're tracking server-side token cost; for the POC we just want to estimate per-1M-token equivalent for both hosted and a Dedicated strip.
[02:24] Samir: We'll provide per-model unit cost estimates and example run cost for your workload; benchmarks will show cost per 1M tokens and cost per successful query.
[02:32] Rita: On compliance: we need to see KMS integration notes and whether logs can be sent to our SIEM; can Redwood redact user PII in logs?
[02:40] Elena: Yes, we support KMS and can show masking/redaction in the runbook. We will not store raw logs beyond the POC unless agreed; also audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM.
[02:50] Samir: Great. Now acceptance test format: we recommend CSV with per-request metrics (latency p50/p95, status code, model variant, batch size), plus a summary PDF that includes charts and a judgement: pass/fail per criterion.
[03:04] Maya: CSV is fine. How will you handle seed randomness for generation so we can reproduce results?
[03:10] Elena: We'll fix seeds and log the model version/hash, quantization profile, and the exact request payloads; that will go into the CSV.
[03:18] Samir: Also we'll provide a runbook that lists exact CLI commands and JMX endpoints if you want to pull metrics.
[03:25] Liam: For network, we'll need an IP allowlist; can you provide ephemeral IPs for the benchmark nodes?
[03:31] Elena: Yes, we'll provide the list ahead of the run.
[03:35] Rita: Also please confirm data retention during the POC — we want logs purged within 30 days and access only to the POC engineers.
[03:43] Samir: We'll configure retention and access controls scoped to the POC, noted.
[03:48] Elena: Ok, walk through of the actual success criteria doc — I have it on screen, I'll read out the acceptance tests.
[03:55] [Screen share starts, small echo/typing noises]
[04:05] Elena: Test 1: Latency — run three baseline windows: short prompt (avg 60 tokens), medium (avg 180 tokens), long (avg 600 tokens). For each window measure p50, p95, and 99. Pass threshold: p95 <= 700ms (medium), p95 <= 1200ms (long), p50 <= 200ms across all.
[04:28] Maya: If we fail p95 by 10%, is that an instant go/no-go? We typically want a tolerance band.
[04:33] Samir: Good question — proposal: if p95 exceeds target by >15% on two consecutive runs we flag as fail; if between 5-15% we mark as degraded and pair with qualitative review. That gives room for infra variance.
[04:48] Liam: We'll need to run multiple runs across different times to avoid noisy windows — what do you recommend?
[04:53] Elena: Recommend three runs per window across two days during your off-peak window; we'll take median metrics to decide.
[05:00] Elena: Test 2: Throughput — sustained 25 RPS for 10 minutes, burst 80 RPS for 2 minutes. Pass if no increase in p95 beyond 30% from baseline and error rate <0.5%.
[05:14] Samir: We should also capture model-side metrics like GPU utilization and batch sizes to understand if batching is saturating.
[05:21] Liam: Please include NVLink saturation and device mem pressure in the report if possible.
[05:26] Elena: We'll include GPU metrics and a short explanation of kernel choices per model variant.
[05:32] Elena: Test 3: Quality — automatic scoring on golden set (BLEU >= 0.6) and manual review pass >= 85%. If automatic fails but manual review passes, we mark as conditional pass and discuss prompt tuning.
[05:44] Maya: We will also run 50 adversarial prompts to check hallucination rates; acceptable hallucination rate <2% on those.
[05:52] Samir: We'll include hallucination checks and flag any open issues.
[05:57] Elena: Test 4: Cost — provide a per-1M token estimate and compare to your current baseline; not a hard fail but part of decision matrix.
[06:06] Maya: Understood. Procurement will weigh cost vs performance.
[06:11] Rita: Security gating: SOC2 cert or equivalent and the ability to rotate keys (HSM preferred). Also we need to ensure logs are scrubbed for user PII prior to any long-term storage.
[06:22] Elena: We have KMS integration and can rotate keys; for PII scrubbing we'll show the redaction pipeline in the runbook.
[06:29] [10 minute mark summary noise — cross talk]
[10:05] Samir: Quick recap of what we'll deliver: finalized success criteria doc, benchmark runbook, sample CSV schema, and SOC2 + network diagram.
[10:14] Maya: Thanks. On timelines we want the POC executed by end of December, decision by first week of January if possible.
[10:21] Samir: That's feasible — proposed schedule: final doc by 12/10, dataset access by 12/11, benchmark runs 12/15-12/18 (avoid your maintenance window), results and summary 12/19, decision meeting 01/06.
[10:36] Liam: Can you confirm Redwood's availability for on-call during benchmark runs? We'll want an SE monitoring channel.
[10:41] Elena: Yes, I'll be on the channel during runs and Samir will join the results call.
[10:46] Maya: A couple minor items: please include a short A/B of model variants (e.g., quantized vs non-quant) and indicate any tradeoffs in latency/quality.
[10:56] Elena: We'll run the benchmark for two model variants (open-1.3x quantized and 1.3x fp16) and include the differences in the report.
[11:04] Samir: For the acceptance PDF, we'll include pass/fail per criterion with a short explanation and recommended mitigations for any fail.
[11:12] Maya: Who signs off? Our PM (not on this call) will review the report and then we can do a joint sign-off; Pioneer legal will not block the POC given SOC2 is provided.
[11:21] Rita: I'll confirm policy but likely InfoSec will provide a final nod after the run and after we've validated retention controls.
[11:27] Samir: Good — so action items again: I'll send the doc and pricing today, Elena will share the runbook and CSV schema, Maya will provide data access, Rita will confirm peering windows.
[11:36] [small typing pause]
[11:40] Maya: One more question around throttling: if Redwood's hosted API hits a quota during the burst test, will you auto-fallback to a lower-cost model or will that count as a failure?
[11:51] Elena: For the POC we'll pin model variants to avoid auto-fallback; fallback behavior will be noted but won't be used during tests. If fallback unexpectedly occurs, we'll count it as a failure unless otherwise agreed.
[12:04] Liam: About observability — can you include per-token timing breakdowns? e.g., tokenization, decode time, KV cache hit rate?
[12:12] Elena: Yes, per-token breakdown and KV cache hit metrics will be part of the CSV. Note sometimes transcripts call KV 'cash' but it's KV cache of course.
[12:21] Samir: Ok last thing: success criteria sign-off process — we'll deliver the raw CSV + PDF and propose a decision matrix: green if all hard thresholds met, yellow if 1-2 soft thresholds missed with mitigations, red otherwise. Decision meeting will include your PM and our AE/SE.
[12:36] Maya: Sounds good. We'll aim to be decisive.
[12:41] Samir: Anything else?
[12:43] Rita: Please make sure the PII redaction examples are included in the runbook.
[12:47] Samir: Will do.
[12:50] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc and calendar invites for the runs.
[12:55] Maya: Thanks all.
[13:00] Meeting end.
